falseFriends.actual: Use 'todellinen' or 'toteutunut', not 'aktuaalinen' (which means 'current/topical' from Swedish 'aktuell')
falseFriends.availability: Use 'käytettävyys' (equipment operational availability) not 'saatavuus' (product obtainability) — critical OEE distinction
falseFriends.performance: Use 'suorituskyky' for general performance; PSK 7501 uses 'nopeus' (speed) for the KNL Performance pillar
falseFriends.stop: Use 'pysähdys' or 'seisokki' for production stop, not 'stoppi' (anglicism/informal)
falseFriends.quality: Use 'laatu' (standard PSK 7501/SAP term), not 'kvaliteetti' (less common synonym that sounds foreign)
falseFriends.billion: Use 'miljardi' (10^9), not 'biljoona' (which means 10^12 in Finnish long scale)

grammarNotes.compoundWords: Finnish merges multi-word English terms into single compounds: 'sykliaika' (cycle time), 'tavoitenopeus' (target speed). Never split: 'sykli aika' is ungrammatical.
grammarNotes.vowelHarmony: Strict vowel harmony: front vowels (ä, ö, y) and back vowels (a, o, u) cannot mix in native stems. Suffixes must match: back-vowel stems get -mat, -kas, -ton; front-vowel stems get -mät, -käs, -tön. Example: 'vuorottomat' (correct, back-vowel stem) NOT 'vuorottomät' (wrong). Neutral vowels (i, e) do not affect harmony.
grammarNotes.caseSystem: 15 cases — nominative for UI labels: 'Käytettävyys'; genitive: 'käytettävyyden laskenta'; partitive for quantities: 'käytettävyyttä 85 %'
grammarNotes.partitiveWithMetrics: OEE values use partitive: 'OEE on 85 prosenttia'. Partitive required after most metric expressions.
grammarNotes.noArticles: Finnish has no articles — do not translate 'the' or 'a/an'. Labels are bare nominative: 'Kojelauta' not '*Se Kojelauta'.
grammarNotes.numberFormatting: Decimal: comma (,). Thousands: non-breaking space. Percentage: '85,5 %' (space before %). Example: 1 234 567,89
grammarNotes.compoundPluralModifiers: In multi-word compound noun phrases, only the HEAD noun pluralizes. The genitive modifier stays SINGULAR — it names the concept/category. CORRECT: 'nopeushäviön syyt' (speed loss [gen.sg] + reasons [nom.pl]). WRONG: 'nopeushäviöiden syyt' (speed losses [gen.pl] + reasons). Same pattern: 'pysähdyksen syyt' (stop [gen.sg] + reasons), not 'pysähdysten syyt'. For single-word compounds like 'nopeushäviöryhmät' (speed loss groups), the compound stem is inherently singular — this is correct by construction.

industryContext.oeeTerminology: Finland has two valid OEE terms: international 'OEE' and Finnish-native 'KNL' (Käytettävyys x Nopeus x Laatu, PSK 7501). Evocon uses OEE. Full Finnish term: 'kokonaistehokkuus'.
industryContext.knlAcronym: KNL = Käytettävyys (availability), Nopeus (speed/performance), Laatu (quality). Defined in PSK 7501:2024. Document as industry context, not as term substitution.
industryContext.dominantSectors: Forest industry (UPM, Stora Enso), machinery (Kone, Wärtsilä, Metso), electronics (Nokia), food, chemicals (Neste)

commonMistakes: Using 'saatavuus' instead of 'käytettävyys' for OEE availability — completely different meaning (supply vs operational)
Splitting compound words: 'syklin aika' instead of 'sykliaika' — compounds always one word in Finnish
Wrong case endings in UI labels — using genitive where nominative required
Using period as decimal separator (85.5%) instead of comma (85,5 %)
Substituting KNL for OEE in Evocon translations — Evocon uses OEE; KNL is documented in industryContext only
Inventing Finnish-only acronyms (e.g. KTT for OOE) — no PSK standard defines these; keep OOE/TEEP as-is

Pluralizing the modifier in compound noun phrases: 'nopeushäviöiden syyt' (WRONG — modifier in genitive plural) instead of 'nopeushäviön syyt' (CORRECT — modifier in genitive singular). The modifier names the category; only the head noun ('syyt') takes the plural
notes: Finnish has both OEE and KNL (PSK 7501) as valid acronyms; Evocon uses OEE. Compound word formation compresses English multi-word terms. 15-case system. Neutral/formal 'te' for B2B. P95 expansion 1.87x.
